question.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $e$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {\frac{{u}^{3/2}}{3/2}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {{(\sqrt{u})}^{3}|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot ({(\sqrt{1})}^{3}-{(\sqrt{0})}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
